newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's terms of trade improved 1.6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Israel's terms of trade improved 1.6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Israel's terms of trade improved 1.6 percent in 1996 after worsening 5.3 percent in 1995 and 2.8 percent in 1994, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
The bureau attributed the turnaround to a sharper drop in import prices than export prices.
Import prices, not counting diamonds or fuel, declined three percent while export prices dropped 1.3 percent, it said.
Prices of imported raw materials fell three percent last year, following a 15.6 percent increase in 1995, while those of imported capital goods dropped 2.6 percent after a 6.3 percent 1995 rise.
The price of imported consumer goods fell 3.7 percent last year, following an eight percent increase in 1995, the bureau said.

It said prices of industrial exports dropped one percent in 1996 following a 5.5 percent 1995 increase. Electronics and telecommunications equipment prices dropped three to four percent while agricultural export prices dropped 6.6 percent after an 8.8 percent increase in 1995.
